title: Residue-field rank criteria for finite-projective maps
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and let $\varphi:P_1\to P_2$ be a homomorphism of finite projective $R$-modules (finite projective means a direct summand of a finite free module). For a prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ write $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ for its residue field. If $\varphi\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is injective, then there is $f\notin\mathfrak p$ such that $\varphi_f:(P_1)_f\to(P_2)_f$ is injective and $\operatorname{Coker}(\varphi)_f$ is finite projective over $R_f$. If $\varphi\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is an isomorphism, then there is $f\notin\mathfrak p$ such that $\varphi_f$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-projective-prime-local-free] to P_1 and P_2 at p. After replacing R by a principal localization R_g with g not in p, both modules are finite free, and the residue-field hypothesis is unchanged because g is invertible in kappa(p).

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-finite-free-map-residue-localization] to the resulting finite-free map. In the injective-fibre case it gives a further principal localization, still away from p, on which the map is injective and its cokernel is finite free, hence finite projective. In the isomorphism-fibre case it gives a localization on which the map is an isomorphism. Composing the two localizations gives the required element f not in the original prime.
